transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Anand, Marco Ruiz (Redwood); Samantha Park, Raj Patel, Lina Gomez (Aquila)

Summary: Quick QBR and technical health check. Discussed usage surge, a couple of reliability blips at peak, roadmap items and next steps for a dedicated pilot + security review.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining the QBR. How are you all doing?
[00:05] Samantha Park: Doing well thanks. Busy week on our side, lots of shipment routing tests.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Great, quick agenda — usage/costs, reliability, roadmap and security, then action items. Priya will cover the technical bits.
[00:20] Priya Anand: Hi all, I'll start with the usage trends — we see Aquila token consumption up ~32% month-over-month, biggest increase on the batch-tracking endpoint. A couple of notes: some prompts are longer, and there's more chat state being retained which increases KV cache usage.
[00:38] Raj Patel: Yeah we added more contextual history to improve accuracy and that probably caused the bump. Any quick read on cost impact?
[00:45] Jordan Lee: From the high level your hosted spend went up about $12k last month, most of it tied to those long-context endpoints. We'll send a per-endpoint breakdown after the call.
[01:02] Samantha Park: We'd like to understand if quantization or a smaller model would keep quality while cutting cost.
[01:10] Priya Anand: Totally. We can run an A/B with a 4-bit quantized variant and measure latency and quality on a subset. For embeddings we can also recommend shorter context windows and prefix caching which reduces repeated tokens.
[01:30] Lina Gomez: On reliability, last Wednesday we saw a p95 jump to ~1.9s from our usual 0.9s for the track-status route during a deployment window. Any root cause?
[01:40] Priya Anand: We traced that to a routing fallback; one of the lower-cost pools briefly lost nodes and traffic routed cross-region, adding latency. We have autoscale/fallback logs. We'll share the trace links.
[01:55] Marco Ruiz: To add, the runtime did a model variant fallback due to a capacity pressure; it was expected behavior but we can tighten the policy so critical endpoints avoid fallback to higher-latency variants.
[02:12] Raj Patel: Can we set stricter routing for the track-status endpoint? We need high consistency.
[02:18] Priya Anand: Yes, you can pin that route to dedicated or a specific region/pool and set fallback to only compatible low-latency variants. That is a config change in the Console or via API. We can propose a dedicated mini-pool for that endpoint as part of the pilot.
[02:40] Samantha Park: What's the lead time for dedicated capacity? We don't want a long procurement delay.
[02:46] Jordan Lee: For a pilot, we can provision a small reserved pool in ~2 weeks if approvals are in place; full production commit is typically a few months depending on size and contract.
[03:02] Samantha Park: Ok. Also, security — Raj has questions about audit logs and KMS.
[03:08] Raj Patel: Yeah we need to ensure keys are customer-managed for the pilot and that audit logs are retained 12 months. Is that supported?
[03:15] Marco Ruiz: Yes, Customer-managed KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated plans, and we can enable extended audit log retention as an add-on. We'll share the security deck and SOC2 artifacts.
[03:30] Priya Anand: One more note on cost — intelligent batching and prefix caching can reduce per-token cost by up to 18% for your workload, per our initial analysis.
[03:40] Samantha Park: That would help. Can you show the estimated savings?
[03:44] Jordan Lee: We'll include estimated savings in the cost breakdown.
[03:49] Priya Anand: Regarding model upgrades — the Redwood team plans to push model v2.1 to hosted in late Q1; we can schedule a canary for Aquila and run your eval prompts to check regressions.
[04:03] Raj Patel: We'd prefer a controlled rollout and regression guardrails.
[04:06] Priya Anand: Absolutely, we can do canary + automatic rollback on quality regression. We also recommend capturing a holdout prompt set for production monitoring.
[04:20] Lina Gomez: On the operational side, we need clearer error codes; sometimes the Console shows generic 5xx without more context.
[04:28] Marco Ruiz: Noted — we'll work with the runtime team to surface more detailed error groups and add a per-route trace link. Expect a follow-up on that.
[04:40] Samantha Park: One more item — latency SLOs. Can we set per-route SLOs in the Console and get alerts?
[04:47] Jordan Lee: Yes, you can configure per-route SLOs and have alerting via PagerDuty/Slack. We'll propose defaults for mission-critical routes.
[04:58] Raj Patel: Competitors — we did a quick bake-off with Megacloud AI and InfraServe; their latency looked similar but billing granularity was worse. Your transparency around per-token cost has helped.
[05:15] Jordan Lee: Appreciate that. We'll keep the cost visibility priority.

Action items recap:
[05:30] Jordan Lee: Jordan to send per-endpoint cost breakdown and token analysis (CSV) by Friday the 20th.
[05:36] Priya Anand: Priya to propose a dedicated pilot config and expected throughput estimates by the 24th.
[05:41] Marco Ruiz: Marco will schedule a security workshop and share SOC2/ISO artifacts and audit log options by the 26th.
[05:48] Samantha Park: Samantha will send the list of internal endpoints and expected Q1 traffic numbers by the 22nd.

[05:55] Raj Patel: Sounds good. Also, please include the suggested quantization A/B test in the pilot plan.
[06:02] Priya Anand: Will do — we'll outline test metrics and evaluation scripts.

[06:10] Jordan Lee: Any other questions?
[06:14] Samantha Park: Not from me, thanks for a thorough review.
[06:18] Raj Patel: No, thanks.
[06:20] Jordan Lee: Great — we'll follow up with the documents and schedule. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
